transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-09
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Rodriguez (Cobalt VP Eng), Tom Everett (Infra Lead), Priya Singh (Security), Arjun Kaur (ML Lead)

Summary (auto): renewal check-in, capacity uplift, EU edge pilot, contract extension options
Topics: capacity sizing, EU edge (private) pilot, SOC2/KMS, pricing and term options, benchmarks

[00:00] Liam (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call — i see Maya, Tom, Priya, Arjun — thanks for making time. we wanted to run through the renewal window, the Q4 scale plan, and the EU edge pilot you mentioned in the last sync.

[00:22] Maya (Cobalt): Yep, thanks Liam. busy week so appreciate it. main thing is we want to lock capacity for holiday ramp and also start a small private/EU-edge pilot for customer sensitive workflows — data residency is the ask.

[00:38] Sofia (Redwood SE): Great. quick clarifying q: when you say "EU-edge" do you mean a private deployment in your VPC in eu-west, or do you want Redwood-hosted regional edges with dedicated capacity? those have different timelines/costs.

[00:55] Tom (Cobalt): Ideally private VPC with our team managing networking — but if the timeline is tight we'd consider Redwood-hosted EU-edge with VPC peering. Procurement is pushing for the former for compliance though.

[01:12] Priya (Cobalt Security): And from security perspective: SOC2 report, attestations, audit logs, KMS integration for key wrapping — those are blockers for private. we asked for SSO/SAML + RBAC as well.

[01:34] Liam: Totally — we can support both. for private we do a customer-managed VPC option and we support KMS/HSM integrations. regarding SOC2 we can share latest report; i'll attach it after the call. side note: some of the product names in our docs occasionally shorten — "Redwood Private" sometimes shows up as "Redwood Pri-" in the draft PDF, ignore that.

[01:55] Arjun (Cobalt): that's fine. main engineering ask is latency — p95 under 200ms for our short prompts, and keep tail latency consistent when we bump batch size. we also want to validate cost per token with quantization turned on.

[02:13] Sofia: okay. two levers to balance: batching to lower unit cost vs. latency. we typically recommend dynamic batching around 8-16 for chat workloads, but with the EU-edge pilot we can configure stricter latency SLOs and smaller max batch size. we'll surface bench numbers.

[02:36] Maya: what's the quickest path to get an isolated environment for pilot? we only need ~4 dedicated GPUs for the first 6 weeks to run traffic mirroring and can ramp to 12 if the perf looks good.

[02:51] Liam: We can provision a 4-GPU dedicated pool in eu-west in ~2-3 weeks if we're doing Redwood-hosted. Private/VPC deployments typically need an onboarding window — usually 4-6 weeks depending on access. procurement timing may push that.

[03:14] Tom: procurement is likely 3 weeks, legal maybe 4-5. so 4-6 weeks for private might work but it's tight.

[03:28] Sofia: For the pilot scope we'll do: traffic mirroring, perf bench (p50/p95/p99), regression detection on a small eval set, and an ops runbook (rollbacks, KV cache priming). i'll make that formal in the runbook.

[03:44] Arjun: Traffic mirroring — that will let us measure real tails without affecting prod yes?

[03:50] Sofia: Exactly. mirror only, no writes. and we can do a canary if you want to test small percent of live traffic.

[04:05] Maya: Pricing — we saw the renewal note — curious about the EU uplift line item. can you walk through numbers?

[04:13] Liam: Sure. high-level: base reserved capacity rate is per-GPU per-hour with commit tiers. EU-hosted edge has +15% uplift due to reserved placement; private/VPC adds an additional one-time onboarding fee and higher per-GPU rate because of isolation. we also offer a 12-month extension discount vs month-to-month. i'll send a revised sheet after this call.

[04:40] Maya: is the uplift negotiable if we commit to 24 months and larger pool?

[04:46] Liam: Yes — we can reduce uplift with a larger term/commit. Southeastern timeline: 12-month gives 10% discount off list; 24-month increases that. We'll model a couple scenarios in the pricing doc.

[05:02] Priya: On the compliance side — audit logs for all inference requests and admin actions are required; can you confirm log retention windows and whether logs can be pushed to our SIEM?

[05:16] Sofia: Logs can be retained per-account with configurable retention; for private/VPC we can either forward logs to your SIEM or give you access to a log bucket. retention defaults to 90 days but we can bump it for enterprise add-on.

[05:33] Tom: For capacity sizing — we'll share peak RPS and token length distribution. what information do you need exactly?

[05:40] Sofia: p95 token length, average tokens per request, peak rps per minute, concurrent requests at p95. that lets us size KV cache and estimate batching benefits.

[05:52] Arjun: We currently see a p95 token length ~220 tokens and peaks at 280 rps in an hour-long daytime surge.

[06:01] Sofia: ok that's helpful. with that profile, dynamic batching at 8-12 should reduce per-token cost by ~15-25% depending on quantization; but p95 latency impact needs testing. we'll run bench scenarios with q4 quantized weights.

[06:18] Maya: any limitations around model variants? we sometimes fallback to smaller models for non-sensitive prompts — can routing be policy-driven?

[06:26] Liam: Yes, smart routing is built-in — you can route by latency SLO, cost tier, or tenant. canary and fallback policies are supported out of the box.

[06:37] Maya: Great. Who typically owns the pilot? is it engineering or success? we want a single contact.

[06:42] Liam: Usually a joint effort — SE leads technical onboarding (Sofia), AE coordinates commercial and procurement (me), and CSM takes over after pilot. i'll loop in our CSM when we land dates.

[06:55] Priya: For KMS — does Redwood support customer-managed keys or only service-managed?

[07:01] Sofia: We support customer-managed KMS for private deployments, including key-rotation policies. for hosted, we offer bring-your-own-key in certain regions — we'll confirm region coverage in the runbook.

[07:13] Tom: On SLAs — what are the SLOs for dedicated pools? we need a 99.9% availability target for production.

[07:20] Liam: Dedicated pools are covered by an SLA that targets 99.95% uptime; we can document penalties in the contract. for pilot we operate best-effort but can include formal SLOs in Dedicated contracts.

[07:33] Arjun: Bench question — if we enable KV cache priming and keep hot prefixes, will that reduce tail lat?

[07:40] Sofia: Yes, priming the KV for common prefixes reduces first-token latency and lowers overall compute. we'll include guidance and scripts to prewarm caches in the runbook.

[07:52] Maya: Any competitor considerations? we had a short POC with Anthropic to compare latency, and internally folks suggested building self-hosted for tight compliance.

[08:03] Liam: Understood — Anthropic looked good in your tests for safety and small prompts, but the cost/throughput tradeoffs were different. building self-hosted adds ops burden; our value prop is the unified runtime and ops tooling + predictable cost.

[08:20] Tom: small nit — can you expose per-route token breakdown in logs? That helps attribution.

[08:25] Sofia: yes, we have token-level breakdowns and per-route cost attribution in the console; we'll share screenshots in the benchmark doc.

[08:36] Maya: ok let's talk timeline: we need pilot started by Oct 15 to validate before holiday ramp. is that feasible?

[08:43] Liam: For Redwood-hosted EU-edge: yes, if procurement signs off quickly. for private VPC, it depends on networking approvals — normally 4-6 weeks. to hit Oct 15 we need signed SOW and PO by Sep 22.

[09:00] Priya: legal needs to review DPA and data processing addendum — can you send standard DPA?

[09:06] Liam: I'll attach the DPA and SOC2 link after the call.

[09:12] Sofia: i'll also send a small bench spreadsheet with prefilled scenarios for dynamic batches 4/8/16 and quantization on/off. that should give quick cost/latency estimates.

[09:22] Arjun: for the pilot runbook — can you include success criteria? we'd say: p95 latency < 200ms for short prompts, error rate < 0.1%, and cost per 1k tokens within 20% of projected numbers.

[09:36] Sofia: absolutely — we'll include measurable success criteria and rollback points.

[09:45] Maya: if we extend the contract 12 months, can we secure additional burst capacity credits? sometimes we need short bursts for campaigns.

[09:53] Liam: yes bursts can be built into the contract as reserved burst buckets or negotiated elastic credits. we'll model that in pricing.

[10:05] Tom: on telemetry — we want real-time tracing hooks for incidents. does Redwood integrate with our datadog/new relic?

[10:12] Sofia: yes we have tracing hooks and can push traces to Datadog; integration details will be in the runbook.

[10:24] Maya: i think that's most of our questions. let's recap next steps.

[10:28] Liam: recap: Liam sends revised pricing with EU uplift and 12/24 month scenarios; Sofia sends bench sheet + pilot runbook with success criteria; Tom sends traffic profile; Maya confirms procurement timeline; we'll aim to get SOW signed by 2025-09-22 to start pilot by Oct 15.

[10:46] Maya: sounds good. one last thing — can we get a short 1-hour workshop for infra & security to walk the team through network setup and KMS?

[10:55] Liam: yes, we'll schedule a 1-hour hands-on session during the week of Sep 22.

[11:03] Priya: thanks all.

[11:06] Liam: thanks everyone. i'll follow up with notes and attachments.

[11:10] End of meeting.
